answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms and renew_incumbent cannot deliver the mandated 18% cut; defer_decision is untenable with the contract expiring in 14 days and no auto-renewal. memory_c2 records that the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, making a switch the most credible path to the cost target. However, the line runs at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so delivery risk is acute: I want to verify c2 (does the archived record support fast, reliable onboarding under time pressure?) and c4 (does the negotiation record suggest any residual leverage with the incumbent worth one last attempt before switching?). The switch should be staged as a guarded transition with overlapping coverage rather than a hard cutover, and adding a second source (c3) should be queued for the next review to protect against the new single point of failure.
